description:
Found 2026-08-14 while trimming the 1-corrector arm out of physics::tests::the_plant_outer_correctors_converge (maintainer instruction).

MEASURED, on the 60 s flow-ramp transient at the 0.1 s plant timestep, twice, deterministic:
  2 correctors : P = 1.77974 MW, T_out = 905.0576 K, T_bed = 905.4925 K, T_steam = 577.9498 K, Q = 7.00539 MW
  3 correctors : P = 1.78319 MW, T_out = 905.0436 K, T_bed = 905.4773 K, T_steam = 607.2434 K, Q = 6.98644 MW
  moved by     : dT_out = -0.014 K, dT_steam = +29.294 K, dQ = -0.271%

PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS' doc table records the 3-vs-2 step as dT_steam = -0.0007 K (measured 2026-08-13). It is now +29.29 K -- about four orders of magnitude larger, and in the opposite direction. The claim 'the loop has converged at 2' is false as things stand.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT. The sweep is PRINTED, never asserted on. The only assertions in that test compare the 0.1 s 'shipped' leg against a 1 ms 'reference' leg, and BOTH legs run at PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS = 2 -- so a corrector-count error is common-mode between them and cancels exactly. Measured the same day, those two legs agree to dT_steam = -0.268 K and the test passes green. A timestep-refinement study cannot detect an unconverged corrector loop; only the sweep can, and nothing checks it.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE 2026-08-14 SECOND-LAW CATCH recorded in the crate CLAUDE.md: a number sitting in a passing test's printed output, in a doc comment, unasserted.

WHAT TO DO (maintainer decision, do not guess):
1. Find out WHAT CHANGED since 2026-08-13. The transient itself also moved (T_out 949.67 -> 905.06 K, T_steam 575.52 -> 577.95 K, P 12.17 -> 1.78 MW), so this is downstream of the kinetics coolant-sink work or the steam-generator changes, not a fresh regression in the corrector loop alone.
2. Decide whether PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS should rise, or whether the 29 K is itself the bug (a 29 K jump from one extra Picard sweep suggests the loop is diverging or bistable on the steam side, not merely under-converged -- note the duty moves only -0.27% while steam moves +5%).
3. ASSERT the sweep. Whatever the converged count turns out to be, the last step of the sweep must be checked against a tolerance, or this recurs silently.

Do NOT simply bump PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS to 3 -- nothing here shows 3 is converged either; the sweep stops there.
title: htgr_sim_v1: the plant outer-corrector loop is NOT converged at 2 -- a third corrector moves the steam outlet 29.3 K

description: Follow-up to op-6tz.18. The depletion burnup loop currently uses one-group cross sections at 0.0253 eV and a one-group infinite-medium k_inf, so absolute k is not comparable to depletion.ipynb's continuous-energy pin-cell MC k (~1.46). Upgrade: tally a multigroup (or continuous-energy) flux spectrum from a real transport solve on a moderated pin-cell geometry (reuse the LIVE pincell CSG), average the njoy cross sections over that spectrum per nuclide, and feed those spectrum-averaged reaction rates into DepletionChain::build_matrix. Then the burnup k should track the notebook's absolute values, not just the trend.
title: outram-mc: multigroup transport-coupled burnup rates (notebook-comparable depletion k)

description:
During the 2026-08-11 Octave control-package z-domain port (see the z-domain follow-ups bead), dlqr/dare/dlyap were deliberately NOT started, per the port's scoping instruction. Reason: upstream inst/dare.m, inst/dlqr.m, inst/dlyap.m sit on SLICOT Riccati/Sylvester solvers (SG02AD, SB03MD, SB04QD families) — a large dense numerical-linear-algebra dependency, and BSD 3-Clause licensed (the SLICOT side of the mixed-licence package, notices must be retained verbatim if ever ported).

DECISION NEEDED before any work: does this crate actually need discrete LQR/Riccati? Its purpose is real-time PID/transfer-function simulation; LQR state-feedback design may belong elsewhere (or nowhere) in the workspace. If yes, the port is a substantial project: general eigenvalue machinery, structured Schur solvers, and careful BSD-3 notice retention per file. Do not start this casually as part of another task.
title: chem-eng: discrete Riccati/Lyapunov (dlqr, dare, dlyap) NOT ported — SLICOT dependency, scope decision needed

notes.content: Do NOT translate HDF5 from scratch and do NOT use C libhdf5. The workspace already ships a pure-Rust HDF5: hdf5-pure v0.20.0 (root [workspace.dependencies], used by njoy-outram-park-fork via hdf5-pure.workspace = true to read real WMP_Library / OpenMC .h5 files). It is pure-Rust and Android-clean, so pflotran HDF5 I/O should depend on hdf5-pure. This removes op-v6s.15.11 from the 'outside the pure-Rust/Android envelope' list -- it is feasible and Android-buildable. (Maintainer directive 2026-07-23.)

title: HDF5 I/O (input + output)
